newsitem.title: USA: Illinois Power nuclear plant faces fine.
newsitem.headline: Illinois Power nuclear plant faces fine.

text.p: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission said Tuesday it proposed fining Illinois Power Co $450,000 for alleged violation of safety requirements at the company's Clinton Nuclear Power Station.

The company violated safety rules during a shutdown in September when company managers tried to keep the plant running instead of taking a safer approach of shutting it down, the federal regulator said.
The commission said its inspection showed Illinois Power employees violated procedures while tyring to reduce a leak from a recirculation pump seal in order to keep the plant operating.

"The violations demonstrate a lack of conservative decision-making, pervasive procedural adherence problems, inappropriate procedures and a lack of rigor in conducting routine plant activities," said NRC Regional Administrator A. Bill Beach in a statement.
The commission proposed fining Illinois $200,000 for the alleged violations during the September shutdown. The rest of the fine would cover 28 other alleged violations, the NRC said.
